brief: Gold is breaking down, trading below its 200-day moving average and testing both the 50-day and the trend line that has held since 2025. A close below that trend line points to $4,000 next. Speculators added a record amount of length across all categories over a three-week period about a month ago, right before gold reversed lower, and that length is now potential fuel for further downside as longs unwind. In China, Shanghai open interest fell 2.6% (11k contracts) as longs liquidated, though Goldman says an onshore EFP position inflates that figure and Chinese specs remain net long. SHFE closes October 1-7 for National Week, so more liquidation is expected into the holiday. Front-end real rates (the 2-year) are near a two-year high while inflation expectations have not risen enough to offset, raising gold's opportunity cost, and higher real yields are hitting the rate-sensitive ETF crowd, with global outflows accelerating. Below $4,000, a level GS says has drawn sovereign and institutional buying, $3,887 is next, then the World Gold Council-highlighted $3,500 area. The note frames this as a short-term setup problem, not a structural break: central banks are still buying about 91 tonnes per month, roughly 5x the pre-2022 pace.
